slides.subtitle: A defensible floor for fixed-price brass export quotes  |  Client: Castle Hardwares, Aligarh (est. 1965)
slides.title: BRASS GUARD

bullets.text: Castle sells hardware to Europe and the Middle East at fixed prices.
But the brass it will buy over the delivery period has no forward price.
So every export quote is priced on gut feel.

slides.notes: The problem in one idea. Owner: quote valid till no price change in market, usually that day only.
slides.title: 1  |  The problem

bullets.text: Buys almost every week, as needed. No bulk buying: too much uncertainty.
A quote holds for a day. Needs at least a one-month projection to plan delivery.
Knows the formula by instinct: LME governs, MCX governs, transport is always extra.

slides.notes: Empathize, Units I-II. Owner intelligence 8/8, recorded verbatim. Ethnography before modelling.
slides.title: 2  |  What the owner actually told us

bullets.text: Brass has no futures market. Price is always built from parts:
INR/kg = copper share + zinc share (via LME x USD-INR) + premium + conversion + freight + duties
72 drivers mapped, 9 proven connections. 2,789 weekly rows (1973-2026) + 955 MCX closes.

slides.notes: Define, Units I and IV. The one formula that matters; everything else is a part, a mover, or a timer.
slides.title: 3  |  Define: one formula, not one number

bullets.text: Forecast the 3 moving legs: LME copper, LME zinc, USD-INR.
Add the slow spreads: premium, conversion, duties.
Output a range, not a number: weekly low / middle / high bands.

slides.notes: Ideate, Units II-III. Divergent options converged into two small models, not one big one.
slides.title: 4  |  The idea we prototyped

bullets.text: Weekly band + quote floor. Same-day Rs 950.40  |  15-day Rs 964.61  |  30-day Rs 972.54
Working backend: 12 modules, 14 endpoints, 47 tests passing. Manual-assist feeds by design.

slides.notes: Prototype, Unit V rapid prototyping. Localhost demo available; figures are this week's band and floor.
slides.title: 5  |  Prototype: Brass Guard today

bullets.text: 8 models trained. Every one lost to the naive carry-forward (DM -5.6 to -10.2).
Buy/wait signal backtested over 1,592 weeks: minus Rs 0.11/kg. Withdrawn.
We killed our favourite features on evidence. The bands survived.

slides.notes: Test, Unit V formative feedback. The honest slide: forecasting rejected, spread layer measured at 0.876 +- 0.039.
slides.title: 6  |  What the tests killed

bullets.text: Units I-II (Empathize): owner interviews, verbatim quotes.
Units III-IV (Define): formula + driver map + honest validation, no future leaks.
Unit V (Prototype + Test): weekly band, floor, iterations. Next: regime buckets + one Castle invoice.

slides.notes: Synthesis. Each syllabus unit maps to a project stage; iteration is the current loop.
slides.title: 7  |  How this maps to the DTPS syllabus

bullets.text: One Castle invoice (Rs/kg, month, grade): turns the market price into Castle's price.
